newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -BTPs vols sag, Bunds firm after Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -BTPs vols sag, Bunds firm after Greenspan.

text.p: BTP option volatilities slid further on Wednesday as futures prices hiked to new peaks fuelled by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments.

Bund options were quiet but one Swiss bank was taking profits in September in-the-money calls from an opening squeeze in futures. At the short-end, December Euromarks saw large buying orders pushing vols up.
"People are generally positive, although they are concerned about the dollar/mark," said one options dealer at a Japanese house in London.

"You'll probably see the 10-year T-note outperform Bunds, there will be pressure on the front part of the Euromarks, and vols will trade firmer," he said, adding that Eurolira vols would drop closer to Euromark vols.
In his semi-annual address to the U.S. Congress on Tuesday, Greenspan said the U.S. growth was slowing for now and that he was reasonably confident inflation in 1997 would be quite modest.
His comments sent bonds, shares and the dollar spiralling higher. Attention is now on Greenspan's second-leg of testimony to the Senate at 1400 GMT.

Dollar/mark hovered below 1.83 after setting 71-month highs. Mark's weakness, due to soft euro perceptions, sparked renewed talk about a Bundesbank intervention, but most traders said this was unlikely.
With August Bund options due to expire on Thursday, September snapped up most of the activity. The at-the-money 103.50 strike was quoted at 4.85 percent vol, up from 4.80 on Tuesday, traders said.
On BTPs, September 140.00 calls attracted some buying, trading at 6.33 percent vol. At-the-money 138.00 BTP straddle was slightly easier at 6.54 percent from 6.60 on Tuesday.
Luke White, broker at Fimat Futures in London, said 136.00 and 137.00 BTP put strikes saw two-way interest and volatility was up slightly on the day at 6.93 percent.
In futures, September Bunds were up 0.21 at 103.24 by 1250 GMT, off a session high of 103.52, while September BTPs gained 0.61 on the day at 138.18, also paring from an earlier record high of 138.44.
At the short end of options, traders said June Eurolira vols on 93.50-93.75 calls were trading cheaper at 19.5 percent, compared with 20.46 at the close on Tuesday.
December Euromarks saw large buying orders at 96.50-96.75 call strikes, with vol trading just under 15.00 percent, traders said.
